questions.stem: All of the following mentioned antibody was seen in dermatomyositis except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Anti CV2
  • Anti-CV2 antibodies are not commonly found in dermatomyositis.
  • Instead, they are more commonly associated with a paraneoplastic syndrome known as encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM), which is a rare neurological disorder characterized by stiffness, rigidity, and involuntary muscle movements. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 844

questions.stem: Which of the following is a typical histological finding in dermatomyositis?

options.label: D
options.text: Perivascular inflammation with muscle fiber necrosis

questions.answerText: Perivascular inflammation with muscle fiber necrosis
questions.solutionHtml:
Perivascular inflammation with muscle fiber necrosis
  • Perivascular inflammation with muscle fiber necrosis is a typical feature of dermatomyositis.
  • There is inflammation around small blood vessels (perivascular inflammation) in the muscle tissue, leading to damage and necrosis of the muscle fibers.
  • This can result in weakness and wasting of the affected muscles. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 844

questions.stem: Gottron patch and heliotrope rash are seen in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Dermatomyositis
  • Gottron's patches and heliotrope rash are classic cutaneous features seen in dermatomyositis. 





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 844

questions.stem: All of the following are histological features of polymyositis except:

options.label: A
options.text: Inflammatory infiltrate was seen in the endomysial region

questions.solutionHtml:
Perifascicular atrophy
  • Perifascicular atrophy is a histological feature typically seen in dermatomyositis, not polymyositis.
  • Polymyositis is a type of inflammatory myopathy characterized by inflammatory infiltrates in the endomysial region of skeletal muscle fibers, leading to degenerating necrosis of myofibers and subsequent regeneration. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 844

questions.stem: All of the following are features of inclusion body myositis except:

options.label: A
options.text: Endomysial inflammatory infiltrate composed of polymorphs

options.label: C
options.text: Admixture of degenerative and regenerative myofiber

questions.answerText: Endomysial inflammatory infiltrate composed of polymorphs
questions.solutionHtml:
Endomysial inflammatory infiltrate composed of polymorphs
  • Inclusion body myositis (IBM) is characterized by the presence of endomysial inflammatory infiltrates primarily composed of CD8+ T cells, not polymorphs. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 844

questions.stem: What is the inheritance pattern of Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
questions.solutionHtml:
X-linked recessive
  • Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 842

questions.stem: Duchenne and Becker's muscular dystrophy is caused by loss of function mutation of-
questions.solutionHtml:
Dystrophin
  • Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy is caused by a loss of function mutation of the dystrophin gene, which is located on the X chromosome. 
  • Dystrophin is a structural protein that helps anchor muscle fibers to the extracellular matrix, and its absence or dysfunction leads to muscle degeneration and weakness, which are the hallmarks of DMD and BMD.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 842

questions.stem: All of the following are histological features of Becker muscular dystrophy except:

options.label: A
options.text: There is segmental degeneration and regeneration of myofibre

options.label: D
options.text: Muscle tissue is replaced by fat and collagen

questions.solutionHtml:
Dense inflammatory infiltrate in endomysial
  • The dense inflammatory infiltrate in the endomysial is not a typical finding in BMD. Inflammatory infiltrates are more commonly seen in autoimmune myopathies or infectious myositis. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 842

questions.stem: Which of the mentioned disease is caused by expansion of CTG triplets repeat?
questions.solutionHtml:
Myotonic dystrophy
  • Myotonic dystrophy is a type of muscular dystrophy caused by an abnormal expansion of a CTG triplet repeat in the DMPK gene on chromosome 19. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 842
